Yesterday, the board of directors of NovaStar—comprised of officials from SummitBridge—was in a strategic meeting and made a series of changes to the board in an effort to confront the deteriorating trend of the corporation. In its report, the board detailed its new strategy, which focused on a global perspective and the reduction of American interests in any strategic direction.

The strategic direction is in line with the widespread intention of the Russian government to ensure the enduring security of American interests, whereby the board saw the necessity of "a new, 21st-century approach" based on a global perspective that would enable mutual economic development and the establishment of mutual technical development. Also, the strategic direction meant that the National Security Agency had adequate measures that allowed the board to ensure the preservation of the technological development. The board’s rationale for the new direction was a response to the weakening of these measures under the old one, which had not seen the effective fulfillment of American technological strategies.

The old board aimed to undermine the strategic development by a strategy that sought to enforce a national focus on American interests, which was entirely seen as a concern by the international community because of a "dangerous" national focus on the destruction of Asian regional powers (i.e. the People's Republic of China) in favor of a new strategic approach.
